zh: 剩余的内存总和等于全部进程的总和减去被删除那一段的和。全部总和是固定的，所以剩余最小，等价于被删除的那段长度为 m 的连续区间之和最大。
长度为 m 的连续段只有 N−m+1 个，起点从 0 到 N−m。用滑动窗口依次得到每个窗口的和：窗口右移一位时加上新进入的数、减去离开的数，记录最大窗口和 best，答案就是 total−best。
读入 N、m 和全部数，同时累加 total。先求前 m 个数之和作为第一个窗口，再对 i 从 m 到 N−1 执行 cur += a[i] − a[i−m] 并更新 best。total 可达约 3×10^15，必须用 64 位整数；N 达到三百万，要用快速读入。m=N 时唯一方案是全删，答案为 0。
en: The remaining memory equals the total of all processes minus the sum of the deleted segment. The overall total is fixed, so minimizing what remains is the same as maximizing the sum of the deleted contiguous segment of length m.

There are only N−m+1 contiguous segments of length m, starting at 0 through N−m. A sliding window yields each window sum in turn: when the window moves one step right, add the number entering and subtract the one leaving, and keep the largest window sum best. The answer is total−best.

Read N, m and all the numbers, accumulating total as you go. Take the sum of the first m numbers as the first window, then for i from m to N−1 do cur += a[i] − a[i−m] and update best. total can reach about 3×10^15, so use 64-bit integers; with N up to three million, use fast input. When m=N the only option is deleting everything, and the answer is 0.

explanationEn:
## Problem

Given the memory usage processes of N processes and an integer m, you must delete exactly one contiguous segment of m processes; find the minimum total memory of the remaining processes after the deletion.

## Derivation

Remaining total = overall total − sum of the deleted segment. The overall total is fixed, so to make the remainder as small as possible, the sum of the deleted contiguous segment of length m must be as large as possible. The answer is total − max(window sum of length m).

## Algorithm

First compute the total, then use a sliding window: the first window is the sum of the first m numbers; after that, each time it moves one step right, add the number that enters and subtract the one that leaves, and record the largest window sum. Finally print total−best.

## Correctness

There are exactly N−m+1 contiguous segments of length m, with starting points 0..N−m. The sliding window obtains the sum of the window for each starting point in turn: going from start i−m to start i−m+1, the window loses a[i−m] and gains a[i]. So best is the largest deleted sum over all possible deletion choices, and total−best is the minimum remaining total. When m=N the only option is deleting everything, and the answer is 0.

## Numeric range

Each number can reach 999999999 and N can reach 3×10^6, so the total is about 3×10^15, beyond the 32-bit integer range; accumulate with 64-bit integers.

## Complexity

O(N) time. The reference reads the input in blocks and parses integers by hand, so that reading the large input does not become the bottleneck.

## Independent verification

The oracle computes every window sum from a prefix-sum array and takes the maximum, without reusing the sliding state; for small domains it also directly sums the remaining elements for every starting point and takes the minimum. All inputs with N=2..6, m=2..N and every number in {2,5,999999999} are enumerated, and the reference program is actually run on each. Large cases cover all values at the maximum (closed-form answer), all values at the minimum, the best window at the start/end/middle, m=N, random large values and more. Four wrong programs that exit normally (32-bit overflow, deleting the smallest segment, a window one too short, deleting only from the two ends) are each judged wrong on the formal cases.
